tasks.short: Establish fabrication procedures for new structural products

steps.what: Determine fabrication methods, machine sequence and constraints for new structural products
Assemble work procedures in the controlled fabrication instruction format
Check fabrication procedures for practical feasibility and submit for authorised review

tasks.design: Configure controlled instruction templates in {DOCS} for assembling a machinist's procedure decisions. The machinist still determines the fabrication method and machine sequence, checks feasibility and submits the proposed version through existing engineering review and trial arrangements.
tasks.previous_blocker: Document assembly can repeat headings, version details and fixed instruction structure.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates can reduce formatting without selecting a fabrication strategy.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing a safe and workable sequence for a new product across several machines.
tasks.human_edge: The machinist anticipates access, distortion and handling issues that a document template cannot determine.
tasks.altitude: Less instruction formatting with procedure judgement and engineering authority unchanged.

reach.task: Review the proposed fabrication sequence and trial requirements
reach.learn: Practical constraints and procedure version control

evidence.claim: Controlled templates can reduce instruction assembly, while novel fabrication decisions and practical checks remain; time allocations are modelled.

assumptions: Boundary is procedure development and submission, excluding engineering authorisation, physical trials and production execution.

Machinist produces operation order, machines, tooling, datums, material, limits and required checks in s1 with all 65 hours retained. s2's 10.5 retained hours include field capture, prose editing and template checks; no structured safe sequence is assumed free.
Missing or ambiguous decisions return to manual engineering clarification. No generated instruction is treated as permission to operate machinery.
Test native templates before custom software. Existing formatting aids earn no new saving. Overlap with general machining-method planning must be allocated once.
unknowns: Actual formatting burden and current procedure templates
research_questions: Can a controlled template shorten assembly without omitting new-product-specific hazards or process checks?

already_counted.description: Field entry, editing and template checks

incremental.description: Maintain controlled templates and revision fields

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=65+10.5+20=95.5; gross 4.5 minus 1 upkeep gives net 3.5. High requires repeated assembly work; low removes only 1 hour, offset by upkeep. Method selection and practical checking retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Clarify clients' materials questions and the finished product's intended use
Locate and check materials information for the specified finished products
Advise clients about materials, limitations and questions needing engineering confirmation

tasks.design: Configure product and revision links to material specifications and available certificates in {DOCS}. The machinist verifies the applicable source, explains the material and its limits, and refers design or certification questions to the authorised engineer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Matching a client's product to the right current material source can interrupt advice.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document links and search filters can reduce repeated retrieval.
tasks.still_hard: Explaining material behaviour in the intended use without overstating certification or design suitability.
tasks.human_edge: The machinist can recognise that a client's question implies a different load or environment from the original design.
tasks.altitude: Less reference hunting; client dialogue and advice boundaries remain intact.

reach.task: Trace an unresolved material question to the authorised engineering source

evidence.claim: Linked material sources can shorten retrieval while suitability interpretation and client advice remain human; the savings are a modelled scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is materials advice, excluding certification, design approval and sales commitments.

Machinist clarifies product and intended use in s1 and captures product identifier, drawing revision, material grade, certificate or batch reference and source version in s2's retained 10.5 hours. No structured client-use classification is assumed.

Engineering and suppliers produce specifications and certificates through unchanged existing work; no new capture is transferred to them. Missing or conflicting traceability requires manual checking and escalation, not an inferred match.
Test native links before custom software. Existing links earn no new gain. All client discussion and explanation retain their time.
research_questions: Can linked material sources shorten retrieval without answering from the wrong product revision or batch?

already_counted.description: Material identification, source capture and applicability checking

incremental.description: Maintain source links and revision traceability

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=20+10.5+65=95.5; gross 4.5 minus 1 upkeep gives net 3.5. High assumes repeated material-source searching; low removes only 1 hour, consumed by upkeep. Client dialogue retains all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce controlled-document assembly and materials-source lookup while keeping fabrication judgement and client explanation personal.
reach: Coordinate with supervisors and engineering reviewers on explicit versions, practical constraints and unresolved materials questions
role.ambitious_version: A machinist who provides clear, traceable procedure proposals and materials advice grounded in actual production constraints.
